title: Derivation of the Tangent Difference Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Continuing from Exercise 55, derive the formula for the tangent of the difference of two angles, \tan(A - B).

steps.title: Substitute -B for B in the Tangent Sum Formula
steps.explanation: Write A - B as A + (-B) and apply the tangent sum formula from Exercise 55.
steps.why: The tangent addition identity holds for any angle, including -B.

steps.title: Use the Odd Symmetry of the Tangent Function
steps.explanation: Since sine is odd and cosine is even, their quotient tangent is an odd function: tan(-B) = -tan B.
steps.why: Dividing an odd function by an even function produces an odd function.

steps.title: Simplify Signs in Numerator and Denominator
steps.explanation: Replace tan(-B) with -tan B to obtain the standard tangent difference formula.
steps.why: In the denominator, 1 - tan A (-tan B) simplifies to 1 + tan A tan B.
